svg.text: Diamond shader — exact behaviour on the real stone D5

src/shaders/diamond/*.glsl · real Ring_v1.glb geometry (597 vertices, 318 triangles) · real gem-000.hdr · shipped uniforms (n 2.42, Δn 0.004, boost 2, γ 1.09, env 1.6, 6 bounces) · one traced pixel, camera 20° off the table normal
normal-capture.vert/frag. From the stone's centre, for every direction:
rgb = outward facet normal·½+½, a = distance to the surface / radius.
Real bake of D5, 256² per face (engine: 512²). Distance range 0.45–1.00.
distance map (a): dark = near, light = far
yellow = rays from the centre (one cube texel each) · pink = stored facet normal at the hit
diamond.frag 158–164, 165–206. The ray refracts at the table (η = 1/2.42),
then loops 6×: TIR (lossless) where the hit angle > 24.41°, exit where < 24.41°.
Real 3D path projected on the view plane (side × table normal).
Find the hit with the cube (not triangles)
intersect(), lines 124–140: sphere guess → plane 1 → plane 2.
Each plane = (cube normal, distance) at the direction from the centre.
Two real bounces: one accurate, one where the cube picked another facet.
white dot = ray origin · cyan = sphere guess · yellow = plane-1 hit
orange = final hit · white ring = exact ray–mesh hit
dashed circle = unit proxy sphere (guess is half-way along the chord)
Attenuation, TIR or exit at every hit
lines 172–173: attenuation *= exp(−dist·κ·(1−color)). line 178: TIR if refract() = 0.
line 202–203: what stays inside *= F·boost. Bars: angle between ray and facet normal.
Critical angle asin(1/2.42) = 24.41°: above it TIR (lossless), below it light exits.
path = canonical units · ×… = absorption of that segment (R channel)
att = running light weight after the hit (R); starts at entry T = 0.825
TIR leaves att unchanged · an exit multiplies the rest by F·boost
lines 196–199: R from refract(n+Δn), G from the exit ray, B from refract(n−Δn).
Plain bilinear texture2D, no blur. Camera-fixed (viewMatrix, line 82).
gem-000.hdr (tone-mapped for display) with the real sample points.
median 0.36: dim base + a few hot spots.
Below: zoomed crops (×8) of the map at
the two exits; dots = R, G, B samples.
Δn = 0.004 keeps the three samples within a fraction of a texel: subtle fire
main(), lines 217–226. Sum of all exits + small front reflection,
then pow(γ) and RGBM-16. The tone-mapping pass (ACES, contrast 1.12)
runs later; the numbers below are for this one pixel.
contrast 1.12 → sRGB OETF: a mid-dark grey facet
tone mapping, bloom (threshold 2.0) and the 32-frame accumulation
are separate passes, not part of the diamond shader
Projected images are of the true 3D data; the CPU bake is 256² Nearest (engine 512²). Nothing here is illustrative.
